text:
1 lawyer with active license to practice law in cities in Yukon-Koyukuk Census Area as of June
D. O. Martin
As of June, cities in Yukon-Koyukuk Census Area had one lawyer in good standing practicing law, according to the Alaska Bar Association.
The number of lawyers that held active licenses in the area remained the same as the previous month.
The only license that was active in the month was granted in the city of Allakaket.
Alaska has no law schools, yet it maintains a higher-than-average ratio of lawyers compared to the relatively low overall population. In Alaska, according to the Bar Association Directory, there are now 2,486 attorneys actively practicing law and a total of approximately 4,160 lawyers licensed to practice in the state.
As of July 2026, average lawyer salaries in Alaska ranged from $108,304 for an entry-level attorney handling routine legal work to $274,458 for highly experienced attorneys managing complex cases with significant autonomy. Mid-level attorneys, such as those in Attorney III roles—who handle highly complex legal work with moderate supervision—earned on average $203,115 in Alaska, compared to $187,635 nationwide.
The United States has more than 1.3 million active lawyers, with employment projected to grow 4% between 2024 and 2034, according to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics.
Data refers to all lawyers who were actively practicing during this period.
